clue.text: Swap made by singular magician

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a witch is a female worker of magic

explanation.surface: A trick exchange pulled off by a one-of-a-kind conjuror.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap two things is to exchange them, a direct synonym of switching.

clue.text: Pole's name sure flummoxed hospital worker

parts.note: a staff is a pole or stick

indicators.note: flummoxed means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Polish man's name baffles someone working on a ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' with a capital suggests a Polish person; it is a stick. 'flummoxed' rearranges N and SURE into NURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff nurse is a qualified registered nurse working in a hospital.

clue.text: Completely at home with everyone

parts.note: at home means in
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Fully relaxed in the house with the whole family.
explanation.definitionFit: In all means altogether or in total, an idiom for completely.

clue.text: "Groggy" rum with cola in demand

indicators.note: groggy means unsteady, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Drinkers clamour for a cocktail of rum and cola that leaves them groggy.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour for something is a loud public demand for it.

clue.text: I kill two turkeys at home

indicators.note: two asks for the turkey synonym to be written twice in a row

parts.note: a turkey is a fool or flop, and so is an ass
at home means in

explanation.surface: A confession from someone who slaughters a couple of birds in their own house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' doubles the synonym for turkeys. The definition is written in the first person: a killer could say 'I kill' of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer could describe their trade in those two words, so the phrase stands for the murderer.

clue.text: Man of high social standing also blowing top

indicators.note: blowing one's top here means losing the first letter

parts.note: as well means also

explanation.surface: A society gentleman loses his temper as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' looks like anger but drops the first letter of AS WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is old slang for a fashionable, well-to-do gentleman.

clue.text: A week at precinct may make one uncomfortable

parts.note: a ward is an electoral or police district, a precinct

explanation.surface: Seven days in a police station would make anyone uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling awkward means feeling embarrassed and ill at ease.

clue.text: A mixture of cider and lager-it could be lethal

definitions.text: A mixture of cider and lager
definitions.meaning: a pub drink made by mixing lager with cider
a venomous serpent's bite can kill

explanation.definitionFit: Snakebite is the name of a cider-and-lager drink and also a serpent's venomous bite.

clue.text: Drama involving lead of snarling chow

indicators.note: involving means one piece holds another inside

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A play featuring an aggressive dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chow' looks like the dog breed, but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow and nosh are both informal words for food.

clue.text: Mark of wound across one hand that's cut — by this?

definitions.text: Mark of wound across one hand that's cut — by this?

indicators.note: the scar piece stretches across the others, holding them

parts.note: a scar is the mark a wound leaves
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: cut means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A scar runs across a hand, with the question of what weapon cut it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's cut' docks the last letter of the hand word, and 'across' wraps the scar word round it and the one. The whole clue also describes what the curved sword does.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sword that could inflict such a wound.

clue.text: Run from farm in a dell in flood

indicators.note: the shortened farm word sits inside the valley phrase

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley, a vale

indicators.note: run taken from the farm word means its abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Water from a flooded farm courses through a little valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' strips the letter for 'Run' off the farm word and 'in' puts the rest inside 'a dell'. 'Run' looks like a verb about water but gives only a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche of letters or complaints is an overwhelming flood of them, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Opening of Kalevala worries poet

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here the epic's title

parts.note: something that worries you eats at you

explanation.surface: The start of the Finnish epic troubles a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kalevala is the Finnish national epic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, so he is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Take in editorial about extremely manly game

parts.note: to take in an argument is to follow it

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a newspaper's leader is its editorial column

explanation.surface: Absorb a newspaper opinion piece about very masculine behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word here, not a container. This is a children's game in which everyone copies whatever the one in front does.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional children's game of copying whatever the leader does.

clue.text: Property not supposed to be taken to car

parts.note: real is genuine, not merely supposed
an estate is a British car with a long rear load space

explanation.surface: Land that is not imaginary being driven to the garage.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is land and buildings, a synonym for property.

clue.text: Perfect state

definitions.meaning: perfect in the sense of complete or total, as in 'a perfect fool'
to state is to say or voice aloud

explanation.definitionFit: Utter means both total (utter nonsense) and to speak, matching each sense.

clue.text: Poor leg spinner — as such, should he be given cap?

definitions.text: Poor leg spinner — as such, should he be given cap?

parts.words: Poor leg spinner — as such, should he be given cap?
parts.note: read as cricket, a weak spin bowler might not earn an international cap; read literally, a balding man needs a hat

explanation.surface: Whether a weak spin bowler deserves selection for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a cap marks selection for a national team, and leg spin is a style of bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin on top means balding, and a poor spinner gives the ball little spin on top.

clue.text: Assess performance of stroke on Hampshire river

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, a county in southern England
a drive is a stroke in golf or cricket

explanation.surface: Judging how well a swimming stroke goes on a southern English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A test drive tries out a car to judge how it performs, an idiomatic match.

clue.text: Perhaps Corydon's dog German lost

indicators.note: lost means a piece is dropped from the dog's name

parts.note: a German shepherd is a dog breed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pastoral character's dog has misplaced its German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corydon's' reads as 'Corydon is'. Corydon is the stock shepherd of pastoral poetry, from Virgil.
explanation.definitionFit: Corydon is a traditional shepherd name in pastoral verse, so he is an example.

clue.text: English poet and Scottish one endlessly feeding pigs

indicators.note: one piece feeding another is going into it

parts.note: swine are pigs

indicators.note: endlessly means losing the final letter

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: Two poets, one English and one Scots, put to work feeding the pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from BURNS to give BURN, which goes into SWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Charles Swinburne was a Victorian English poet, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Dramatist's plot works

parts.note: a plot of garden is a bed
something that works does, as in 'that does'

explanation.surface: A playwright's storyline is effective.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Lovell Beddoes was an English dramatist and poet, an example of a playwright.

clue.text: Indian by lake making a trap

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A Native American sets a trap beside the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket or pot used to trap fish and lobsters.

clue.text: Pirate's reportedly crude song

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a crude song is a coarse air

explanation.surface: A buccaneer is said to sing vulgar shanties.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a pirate, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: What Sauron aimed to be: Marquess of Queensberry?

definitions.meaning: Sauron, Tolkien's villain, wanted to master all the rings of power
the Marquess who gave his name to boxing's rules could be called a master of boxing rings

explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's novel title fits Sauron's ambition, and punningly a nobleman ruling over boxing rings.

clue.text: Father describing bird's bone

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line round, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
the emu is a large flightless bird

explanation.surface: A priest giving an account of a bird's skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone.

clue.text: Lacking judgment, cut out time in local

indicators.note: cut out means a letter is removed

parts.note: a local is a native of a place

explanation.surface: A foolish pub-goer is asked to leave before closing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a pub, but it means a resident.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and inexperienced, lacking sound judgment.

clue.text: Good enough to secure a mandate

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast around another piece

parts.note: fit means suitable, good enough

explanation.surface: Being suitable enough to win an electoral mandate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative order or decree, a mandate.

clue.text: Opening of number covered by funky trio?

indicators.note: one piece covered by another sits inside it
funky suggests a jazzy reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The first bars of a song are played by a groovy three-piece band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like the first-letter signal for 'number', but it is the definition. N goes inside ITRO, an anagram of TRIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a song or piece of music.

clue.text: Drink — a small measure knocked backed by girl

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl downs a small measure of a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses A GRAM to give MARGA; 'backed' is printed for 'back', and 'by' is a link. 'Knocked back' also sounds like downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a tequila cocktail, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Following videos, attempt needlepoint

indicators.note: the attempt piece comes after the videos piece

parts.note: video recordings are tapes
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: After watching instructional videos, someone has a go at embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestry is woven or stitched decorative work, close to needlepoint embroidery.

clue.text: Band's releases we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to release is to free, so releases are frees

explanation.surface: A pop group's new records, as listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band's' reads as 'Band is'; the band is a decorative strip, not a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a horizontal decorative band along a wall.
